subject: Discovery recap & proposed PoC milestones - Avalytics
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Julia Martin <julia.martin@avalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & proposed PoC milestones - Avalytics

Hi Julia,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. I wanted to capture the key pain points you described, confirm success criteria, and propose a concise PoC plan so everyone is aligned. Below is a short recap and suggested next steps. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

Pain points you shared:
- Latency spikes on inference paths during peak shopping hours (10–12ms target, currently 40–70ms for multi-turn flows).
- Cost unpredictability from current setup (per-token costs and duplicate inference work across services).
- Difficulty integrating model updates into release cycles without impacting uptime.

Current stack (as described):
- Frontend: React + Next.js
- Backend: Node + Java microservices (Kubernetes)
- Existing LLMs: self-hosted 7B model on EC2/GPU for re-ranking, vendor API for generation
- Metrics: Datadog for latency, internal event store for tokens and usage

Success criteria for PoC (we aligned on):
1) End-to-end 95th percentile latency <= 25ms for the generation + re-rank path under a synthetic 50 RPS load.
2) Cost-per-session reduction of >= 30% via batching and KV caching.
3) No functional regressions on top-3 production prompts (we’ll validate with the prompt set you shared).

Proposed PoC scope & milestones (4 weeks):
- Week 1: Kickoff, environment access, and telemetry baseline capture (owners: Marissa / Avalytics eng).
- Week 2: Integration of Redwood SDK (Node + Python helper) into a canary route; implement prefix KV cache for common prompts (owner: Karthik).
- Week 3: Load test at 50 RPS, collect latency/cost metrics, iterate on batching window/config.
- Week 4: Final evaluation vs success criteria, rollout recommendations and rollback plan.

SDK & compatibility notes:
- We will provide a lightweight Node SDK sample that fits into your microservice and a Python helper for any offline processing. For Java we can provide a short example using our HTTP client and request signing.

Action items / owners I captured:
- Jul ia: Share prompt set + a short list of 3 production routes to validate by EOD Tue.
- Marissa: Coordinate account & billing info so we can allocate a PoC pool.
- Karthik: Draft onboarding checklist and confirm any firewall/VPC egress requirements.
- Priyom: Share PoC outline and SDK compatibility matrix (attached).

Next meeting: I propose a 30-min technical kickoff on Wed 2027-08-18 at 10:00am PT. Please confirm if that works.

Attachments: redwood-poc-outline.pdf (PoC milestones + evaluation plan), sdk-compatibility-matrix.csv (language/feature matrix).

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

--
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
pri yom.das@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Priyom — this looks great and mirrors what we discussed. A few clarifications: 

- Prompt set: I’ll upload the anonymized prompt set (3 routes + edge cases) to the Drive link by Monday morning.
- Data retention: We need to confirm the default data retention and whether logs can be kept for 30 days for debugging; is that configurable per-customer?
- SDK: Node sample is perfect. We also have a small offline Java service that batches inputs nightly — could you confirm the Java HTTP example covers tokenization/encoding details?

Kickoff time on Wed 2027-08-18 10:00am PT works for Amit (CTO) and me. Please include a dial-in and calendar invite.

Also: we will need a short statement on security controls (SOC2 scope) for procurement — can Marissa start that thread?

Appreciate the concise plan.

Julia
Julia Martin
Head of ML Engineering | Avalytics
julia.martin@avalytics.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & proposed PoC milestones - Avalytics

Quick notes on the technical questions Julia raised: 

- Data retention: Yes — per-tenant retention windows are configurable for logs and trace data at the account level. For PoC we can set 30-day retention and export raw logs if needed. I will add the configuration snippet to the PoC guide.
- Java compat: Our Java example (HTTP client) includes the same canonical tokenizer and the request/response shape matches the Node SDK behavior. I’ll attach a minimal java-example.http and point to where token costs are computed.
- Firewall/VPC: If they want Private deployment we’ll need a customer ticket; for hosted PoC we have IP allowlist and TLS mutual auth options.

I’ll own the onboarding checklist and will share it by EOD Tue so Marissa can start procurement items.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer | Redwood Inference
